Volcanoes, water and expedition sites

This page covers the volcanic ground, the kinds of water you will find, and how to reach and collect the three expedition sites near spawn.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Volcanoes and volcanic ground
  2. Lakes, rivers and wetlands
  3. Expedition sites
  4. How this was checked

Volcanoes and volcanic ground

Some islands have a volcano. Each one has one of three shapes. Volcanoes and volcanic terrain

  • Shield volcano: a broad, low mountain.
  • Stratovolcano: a steeper cone.
  • Breached caldera: a wide summit crater with one side broken open. Calderas are always old and worn down.

Older volcanoes are lower, wider and more overgrown; young ones are bare and hotter. A volcano only forms on an island big enough to hold it, never on an atoll, and the starting island very rarely has one. To find one, search for Volcano in the map locator.

Volcanic ground is made of Basalt, Obsidian, Volcanic ash, Lava rock, Smooth lava rock and Magma stone. Hot springs and geyser basins add Mineral crust, Sulfur crust and Geyser stone.

Magma stone glows, but it does not light up the ground around it. Steam vents sit in the mouths of small vent cones in volcanic fields, calderas, surface lava tubes, hot springs and geyser basins.

Good to know. Nothing here can hurt you: you can walk on magma stone and steam vents and swim in boiling water. Steam vents are plain blocks and do not give off steam.
Planned, not in the game. Molten, flowing lava and fire are not in the game yet. Volcanoes are solid, cooled rock and nothing burns. Lava Fire

Lakes, rivers and wetlands

Islands have river channels, inland lakes, marshes, bogs, mangroves, bayous and frozen lakes. Inland lakes lie between about 6 and 56 m above sea level. Rivers, lakes and wetlands

Water only stands at sea level, in lakes and in small springs and pools. A river channel holds water where it cuts down to sea level; higher up the island its valley is dry.

Natural water stays still: rivers do not flow, and water never pushes you. Only the sea's Water can flow. In Creative, the catalog's Water block spreads and pours over edges, and digging next to the sea lets it run into the gap. The other five kinds of water never flow, even when you dig beside them. See flowing water.

The kind of water depends on where it is:

  • Sea and coasts: Water.
  • Lakes, springs, oases, inland river channels and cooler wetlands: Fresh water.
  • Warm, very wet lowlands such as bayous: Black water.
  • Hot springs and geothermal ground: Hot spring water. The hottest pools are Boiling water.
  • Frozen lakes: Ice or Black ice, with Fresh water underneath. Frozen fjords: Ice, Black ice or Glacier ice. Under Glacier ice the water is Dark fjord water.

You can swim in every kind of water. There is no air meter, so you cannot drown.

You can drink and fill flasks at Water, Fresh water and Hot spring water. Black water, Boiling water and Dark fjord water are not drinkable. Drinking and water flasks (T)

Expedition sites

Worlds of generation 10 or later have three small expedition sites near spawn; new worlds use generation 12. Each site is somewhere inside a square about 120 m wide, on dry, level ground. The squares are centred about 110 m east, 170 m south-west and 220 m north-east of X 0, Z 0, where a new world starts. Expedition sites and one-time supply finds

Good to know. Worlds older than generation 10 have no expedition sites. If the game cannot find a dry, level spot in a square, that site is missing.
  1. Press E, then press Tab until the Journal opens, or click its tab. The three sites are listed under Expeditions. A '?' means you have not found it yet, and a '+' means you have.
  2. Click a site name to make it your destination. A light beacon and an on-screen marker with its distance show the way. Destinations: map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker
  3. Walk to within 12 m of the site and stand on the ground. Flying, sailing or riding does not count. The status line says 'Discovered' and the site name.
  4. While still within 12 m, open the Journal and click Find next to the site. Jumping or swimming is fine, but not flying, sailing or riding; otherwise the game says 'Discover on land; collect nearby without flying or riding'.
  5. If your pack is too full, the game says 'Leave pack space; the find will wait here'. Free some space and try again.
  • Survey workshop: 16 Alder boards and 8 Glass.
  • Reed refuge: 16 Reeds.
  • Stone overlook: 8 Chalk and 8 Basalt.

After you collect a find, the game says 'Find collected | use Craft to turn it into building materials', and its button reads Taken. You can still mine the site's own blocks. In Survival, reaching a site and collecting a find complete the Landmark and Supplies milestones.

Careful. Each find can be collected only once, and the game saves that it was taken. Finds are for solo worlds: on a server the button reads Solo only.

How this guide was checked

Re-checked against the Voxelgame 251b9e46 source on 8 November 2026. Volcano shapes, ages, size limits and the starting-island rule: crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/relief.rs, regions.rs and terrain_profile.rs. Volcanic and geothermal ground and vents: generator/surface.rs, structures.rs and features/vents.rs. Block names: world/block/table.rs. Water kinds, lakes, springs and ice: world/generator.rs, generator/terrain_profile.rs and generator/surface.rs. Water flow: world/mod.rs. Swimming, drinking and damage: world/block.rs, survival.rs and survival/water.rs. Expedition sites, discovery and finds: game/exploration.rs; the Journal labels: crates/voxelgame-render/src/inventory_ui.rs.

Initial ledger audit: Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; article updated 8 November 2026. Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. A site is skipped when its square has no dry, level spot, so some worlds may have fewer than three. The squares and distances are the code's rule; the exact site is somewhere inside its square. Lake heights and water kinds follow generation thresholds and were not measured in a world.
